note: hooks/before_build.py — the anti-rediscovery guard (#105), sibling of the write gate. It rides a build-shaped UserPromptSubmit and injects a two-lens reminder (check the box, then the open internet) with a tree-derived count, pointing at `nestor decision check`, IDEAS §7, and Jeles conflict_scan. Written only after two look-sees confirmed no such hook existed and that the fleet's clustering/scoring primitives already exist (willow-mcp nest/selflearn, Nestor semantic_matcher/calibrate) — a worked instance of its own rule. Recursion caught live: the operator stopped a jump-to-build, which is the exact failure the hook surfaces.

decisions.question: The write gate makes an agent consult before editing. What makes an agent consult before *building* a new thing?
decisions.commitment: before_build, an advisory UserPromptSubmit hook. On a build-shaped prompt (a strong construction verb, or write/add/make/wire next to a construct noun) it injects the anti-rediscovery reminder and stays silent otherwise, so a status question or a seal costs nothing. Its one number — the count of recorded decisions — is globbed from the tree at emit time, never hardcoded. It is wired into the CLI-agnostic runner and .claude/settings.json alongside reinject, and pinned by a prove-it-can-fail test that asserts both directions (fires on a build prompt, silent on a question) plus the on-the-wire contract.
decisions.why: This fleet's largest documented tax is rediscovery — rebuilding an organ that already existed and was often better (the-house-already-knew.md: four in one session). before_write already encodes consult-before-editing; building is where the rediscovery actually happens, and nothing surfaced the box at that moment. Silent-unless-build is the reinject lesson (a reminder every turn is noise); the derived count is the IDEAS §4.5 lesson (a hardcoded number drifts).

decisions.question: Is this a gate?
decisions.commitment: No — advisory, and it says so in its own text: a tripwire, not a boundary. A hook cannot run the survey for an agent or stop it from building; it can only name where to look. So it is excluded from scripts/hook_guard.py's blocking-gate proof (it injects context, it never denies), listed there among the non-gates with reinject and session_end.
decisions.why: Say enforcement or ledger. Selling a reminder as a guard is the overclaim this repo refuses; naming it a tripwire keeps it honest. Its job is to make the box visible at the build moment, not to be unbreakable — the survey is still the agent's to run, and the human's to insist on, as this very session showed.
